answer: Randomized spot-check auditing resists sybils: each epoch a trusted jury re-grades a random sample of every grader's verdicts, and any grader whose sampled grades diverge from the jury triggers a full re-audit. A colluding farm must cast many grades to sway outcomes, yet the more it casts the higher the chance one is sampled — catch probability rises as 1-(1-s)^n toward near-certainty at volume. An honest grader's whisper of a few accurate verdicts rarely trips the sample and passes clean as marble; a cedar-dense thicket of fraud is almost surely caught, so volume becomes the exposure.
